mission: Luke assigns Ben the survey mission along the Outer Rim — both father and son feel the wrongness, but Ben's interpretation differs
why_now: Luke has been monitoring the wrongness independently; the survey is his response — but sending Ben alone is a choice the narrative will interrogate
conflict: Ben wants autonomy; Luke offers the mission as both genuine need and a way to give Ben space. Underneath: Luke's shadow — he chose to send one person to investigate a problem that might require more
turning_point: Luke admits he feels the wrongness too but interprets it differently — Ben's experiential pattern recognition from Jacen, Abeloth, and Vestara gives him a sharper read
opening_hook: Luke's datapad shows a string of survey reports flagged with the same anomaly — Force readings that don't match any known phenomenon
closing_hook: Ben accepts the mission without suggesting a partner. Luke doesn't push. Neither acknowledges what that choice means.
emotional_trajectory: Guarded attentiveness -> brief connection with Luke -> deliberate distance

stakes.personal: Ben's need to prove himself independently of Luke's shadow
stakes.interpersonal: The careful, love-laden distance between father and son
stakes.external: The survey route runs directly along the wrongness's bearing

setting: Luke's office in the Jedi Temple, Coruscant — functional, lived-in, holocomm on the desk
sensory_details: Luke's Force presence — vast, warm, familiar; the datapad's blue glow; the wrongness present even here, a faint sourness under the Temple's harmonics
canon_elements_needed: Luke Skywalker as Grand Master of the Jedi Order
Jedi Order survey mission protocols and assignment hierarchy
Luke and Ben Skywalker relationship post-Lost Tribe crisis
Force perception differences between Skywalker bloodline practitioners
Jedi Temple Grand Master administrative spaces
action_beats: Luke slides the datapad across the desk showing seventeen flagged survey reports
Ben scrolls through the anomaly data, zooming on three readings that match his own perception
Ben sets the datapad down and moves to the window — body language of someone accepting a solo mission
promises_planted: Luke sent Ben alone — the irony will become apparent (PP12)
Ben's unique Force perception will resolve into something meaningful (PP22)
notes: Luke should feel warm but slightly distant — they love each other but communicate through mission briefings. Ben thinks 'Dad' internally but acts like a professional.
